Title: MACC postpones recording of Isa Samad's statement over health
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has postponed recording the statement of former Felda chairman Datuk Seri Isa Samad until his health improves.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said Isa was currently receiving treatment at Serdang Hospital after undergoing eye surgery.
"Regarding Isa's statement, we had to put it on hold as it was supposed to be recorded yesterday and today. However, as he was unwell and was sent to Serdang Hospital for eye surgery, we have postponed it for now.
"We will resume recording his statement after receiving an update on his health status from the Prisons Department.
"Once he has recovered, we will continue recording his statement. There is still a lot that needs to be recorded from him," he said.

Title: Two Myanmar nationals held after allegedly assaulting policeman
Article:
RAUB: Two Myanmar nationals were arrested after allegedly assaulting a policeman who had reprimanded them for playing loud music by the roadside at Kampung Pamah Kulat in Dong here early today.
The suspects, aged 26 and 30, who work at a plantation, were also drunk
during the 2.45am incident.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a corporal, was alerted by villagers before going to the scene to conduct checks.
"Both suspects were drunk and had been causing a nuisance by playing loud music by the roadside. When the policeman reprimanded them, they became angry and began assaulting him.
"The assault caused the victim to suffer swelling to his head and body. He is warded at Raub Hospital for treatment," he said.
Azry said both suspects were detained shortly after the incident.
No weapons were used in the attack, he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 353 of the Penal Code for using criminal force against a public servant in the execution of his duties.
The offence carries a maximum two-year jail term or a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.

Title: MG S5 packs strong value into an electric SUV
Article:
THE MG S5 EV has become one of the more interesting electric SUVs in Malaysia, particularly after its transition from fully imported (CBU) to locally assembled (CKD) production thie year.
The latest version is priced from around RM116,900 and brings substantially more power, improved equipment and a longer claimed driving range.
At first glance, the S5 EV does not look radically different from the growing number of electric SUVs on Malaysian roads.
It is a compact five-seat crossover with a clean, contemporary design.
However, one of its biggest selling points is hidden underneath: rear-wheel drive.
Unlike many similarly priced EVs that use front- or rear-biased configurations depending on the platform, the S5's RWD layout gives it a more balanced driving character and helps distinguish it from rivals.
POWERTRAIN
For 2026, MG has upgraded the S5's powertrain considerably.
The locally assembled S5 EV LUX Long Range produces 203PS and 350Nm, compared with 170PS and 250Nm in the earlier CBU model.
It uses a 62kWh LFP battery and claims up to 446km of WLTP range, while 0-100kph takes about seven seconds.
On Malaysian roads, that combination makes the S5 EV feel considerably more energetic than its sensible family-SUV appearance suggests.
Range is another major strength.
The official 446km WLTP figure is competitive for an EV in this price bracket, although real-world range will naturally depend on speed, traffic, weather and air-conditioning use.
For Malaysian owners, that should still translate into enough range for normal commuting without constantly thinking about charging.
Long-distance travel is helped by the S5 EV's 150kW DC fast-charging capability.
MG claims a 10-80 per cent charge can take about 26 minutes under optimal conditions.
At home, however, AC charging is limited to 7kW, so owners without DC charging access will need to plan around overnight charging.
INTERIOR
Inside, the S5 EV offers a surprisingly comprehensive equipment list.
The LUX gets a 10.25-inch digital instrument display, a 12.8-inch infotainment screen, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, wireless phone charging, six speakers, a powered tailgate and a panoramic sunroof.
There is also a 360-degree camera, which is particularly useful in tight Malaysian parking spaces.
Practicality is equally convincing. The S5 has 453 litres of boot space, expanding to 1,441 litres with the rear seats folded.
That makes it suitable for a small family, although buyers needing maximum rear-seat or cargo capacity may still find larger SUVs more accommodating.
STRONG POINTS
The biggest question is whether MG's ownership proposition can match the car itself.
The S5 EV offers impressive specifications for the money, but buyers should consider MG's developing Malaysian aftersales and charging ecosystem alongside established competitors.
Safety equipment is another strong point.
The car comes with seven airbags and a broad suite of driver-assistance systems, including adaptive cruise control, autonomous emergency braking, lane-keeping assistance, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert and traffic-jam assist.
The move to local assembly in Melaka is encouraging, however, and represents a meaningful step in MG's longer-term commitment to Malaysia.
THE DRIVE
The S5 EV delivers a confident and enjoyable driving experience, combining the instant response of an electric motor with the balance of rear-wheel drive.
With 203PS and 350Nm of torque, acceleration is brisk, making it easy to merge onto highways or overtake slower traffic.
Instant electric torque makes city acceleration effortless, while the RWD configuration gives the car a more natural feel when accelerating out of corners.
The power delivery is smooth rather than aggressive, so the S5 remains easy to control in daily driving.
Its multi-link rear suspension helps provide a comfortable ride over Malaysia's uneven roads while keeping the SUV composed through corners.
Steering is light and effortless at low speeds, making city navigation and parking convenient, although it offers little feedback for enthusiastic drivers.
At highway speeds, the S5 EV feels stable and planted, with good refinement and minimal drivetrain noise.
It is not intended to be a sports car, but the S5 is arguably more enjoyable to drive than its price and practical positioning would suggest.
VERDICT
Overall, the MG S5 EV is an easy car to recommend on paper and a particularly compelling option for buyers wanting an EV that combines performance, range, equipment and value.
Its RWD layout gives it an advantage in driving character, while the 62kWh battery and 446km WLTP range make it practical for everyday Malaysian use.
At roughly RM117,000, the CKD model is difficult to ignore.
It may not have the strongest brand presence in Malaysia, but the MG S5 EV demonstrates that an affordable electric SUV does not have to be boring.
For buyers ready to switch to electric, it deserves a serious place on the test-drive list.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMA calls for stronger healthcare workforce measures in Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has urged the government to prioritise healthcare workforce retention, stronger screening and follow-up care, and greater private-sector involvement in Budget 2027.
Its newly appointed president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan said Malaysia could not afford to wait until workforce shortages became more severe, citing data showing that 3,494 doctors left the Health Ministry between 2019 and 2023.
"Malaysia is already short of nearly 11,000 specialists, while nursing vacancies stand at about 18 per cent.
"Only 529 housemanship positions offered in January 2026 were filled, and every unfilled post adds pressure to an already stretched workforce and risks further weakening the capacity of public healthcare to provide timely and quality care," he said in a statement today.
Sivanaesan said the government must allocate sufficient funding for its plan to abolish the contract system and offer eligible house officers permanent positions upon completing housemanship by 2028.
He also called for previous years of contract service to be recognised for seniority and salary progression.
For specialists, MMA proposed a transparent, merit-based pathway for experienced doctors to progress to Gred Khas or Gred Utama C after at least five years of satisfactory service following gazettement.
"Promotion should not be automatic. MMA proposes an assessment based on 80 per cent objective and measurable criteria and 20 per cent structured professional assessment.
"By the 10th year following gazettement, every specialist recognised as a Medical Consultant should have undergone a formal promotion assessment, with the outcome and reasons clearly communicated," he said.
Sivanaesan said Budget 2027 should also address policies that made it harder for doctors and specialists to build sustainable careers in public healthcare.
Among the measures proposed were a review of the requirement for three consecutive complete Annual Performance Assessment Reports before subspecialty training, sufficient Jawatan Simpanan Latihan, specialist allowances from the date of gazettement and fair on-call rates for doctors performing specialist responsibilities.
On the Flying Doctor Service (FDS), Dr Sivanaesan called for increased funding to ensure adequate maintenance and the service's sustainability, including equipment, aircraft support and operational requirements.
He also called for a substantial review and increase in FDS personnel allowances, which he said had remained unchanged since 1978.
On primary care, Sivanaesan called for greater investment in the prevention and early detection of non-communicable diseases, including diabetes and hypertension, to reduce complications and ease pressure on hospitals.
"Budget 2027 should fund treatment and monitoring following government-supported screening, using Malaysia's network of more than 11,000 private GP clinics," he said.
MMA also proposed the establishment of a Private Healthcare Development Division within the Health Ministry to coordinate the private healthcare sector, complementing the regulatory role of the Medical Practice Division (CKAPS).
The association also proposed RM10 million to digitise CKAPS registration and licensing processes through a single online platform.

Title: Easy money: Man loses RM301,777 to scam by mystery sender in whatsapp
Article:
TEMERLOH: A  plantation worker lost RM301,777 after falling victim to a bogus investment scheme sent to him through an anonymous WhatsApp message, police said.
The 51-year-old oil palm worker from Kuala Krau not only used his savings, but also borrowed money from his siblings and friends to participate in the scheme.
Temerloh police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the victim claimed that he received the message from an unknown number on Aug 11.
"The 'Prestige Prime' scheme lured him with promises of high returns, and he believed it would help increase his income.
"He clicked on a link to register and was then told to start making investments.
"The victim made 18 transactions amounting to RM301,777 into nine bank accounts. He used his savings and borrowed money from a younger sibling and friends,"  Nasyim said in a statement today.
According to Nasyim, the victim later discovered that his investment account was blocked and realised he had been cheated.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a jail term of up to 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three days of fun, entertainment at Jom Heboh Segulai Sejalai Sarawak
Article:
MIRI: Karnival Jom Heboh Segulai Sejalai Sarawak 2026 returns to Sarawak after a 19-year absence, with the three-day event starting at Miri Boulevard today.
Organised in collaboration with the Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Ministry, the carnival features a range of entertainment, recreational and interactive activities throughout the three days.
The event is expected to attract about 300,000 visitors from across Sarawak and neighbouring countries, with 160 booths featuring various organisations, agencies and other participants.
The booths will give visitors opportunities to enjoy entertainment, obtain information, take part in interactive activities and access services offered throughout the carnival.
Among the booths attracting attention on the first day are those by the Miri district police headquarters, led by Superintendent Mohd Syafiq Jinuin Abdullah, and the Police Family Association (Perkep), headed by Arabiah Abdulrahim.
The Health Ministry is also offering dental services to visitors, alongside other health-related activities.
[[nid:1541041]]
The opening day features a light exercise session with the Health Ministry at the main stage at 8.30am, followed by a children's colouring activity at Studio Tonton Drama Sangat.
Visitors can also catch the Buletin Challenge featuring Fahiz, Shafiq Adnan, Afrina Romzi and Saree Abdullah, while Jom Lokal Jam is scheduled for 9pm at the main stage.
Tomorrow's activities include a children's traditional costume competition at 10.30am, the Ratu Etnik competition at 11am, Buletin Challenge at 3pm and Meet & Greet Drama Sangat at 4pm.
The highlight of the second day will be the Jom Heboh Segulai Sejalai Sarawak Concert at 9pm, featuring KOI, Marygrace, Fieya Julia, Nabila Razali and Man Bai.
The carnival continues until Sunday with activities for the whole family, including the Jom Heboh Fun Run "Lari Baik Baik Bersama EPF" at 8am.

Title: Two expected to face charges over Kedah fertiliser distribution
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Two people are expected to be charged over alleged irregularities involving the distribution of fertiliser to farmers in Kedah.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigation into the matter had been completed and the case classified under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
"The MACC prosecution division will refer the case to the Attorney-General for further action.
"If the Attorney-General gives consent based on our recommendation, the charges may be registered in court next week or the following week," he said at a press conference today.

Title: Two ex-Felda officers to be charged over KLVC project
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Two former senior Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) officials being investigated over alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project will be charged next week.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the Attorney-General had given consent yesterday to prosecute the two.
"The former Felda general manager will face one charge under Section 420, and the charge will be registered at the court on Sept 30, which is Wednesday.
"Meanwhile, the other person, the former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Commission, will face two charges under Section 417, and the charges will be brought on Sept 29," he said at a press conference today.

Title: Saravanan, family ordered to declare assets to MACC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Former Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan, his wife and their three children have been ordered to declare their assets to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said notices under Section 36 of the MACC Act would be served on Saravanan, his wife and two of their children at the MACC headquarters on Monday, while another child studying in London would receive the notice in November.
"Saravanan, his wife and two of their children would be present at the MACC headquarters to receive the notices, while another child who is studying in London would receive the notice in November.
"The notices will be served on him, his wife and his three children this Monday. They have been informed and will come to the MACC headquarters for the notices to be served," he said at a press conference today.

Title: Witness confirms seeing confidential email to Petros top officials, but unsure of sender
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A witness told the Sessions Court here today that she had seen the email containing Petronas confidential documents that was sent to two senior officials of Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros).
Petronas human resources division manager Suhaidah Labu, 42, said she saw the email, which was allegedly sent by former manager Mohd Khairul Akmal Mohd Jasni to Petros chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Janin Girie and chief financial officer (CFO) Azha Jalil Abdul Jalil.
The sixth prosecution witness said the contents of the email included, among others, an operational and financial performance report for the first quarter of 2024 dated May 10, 2024.
She said the email was presented to her by Petronas industrial relations officers Jumsuri Basri and Zatil 'Ismah Azmi on Dec 6, 2024.
"They contacted me to obtain confirmation on whether Khairul Akmal had resigned.
"This was because, in the email, Khairul Akmal stated, 'I look forward to joining your team.'
"After I checked his records in the system, I found that there was no record of his resignation and he was still an active Petronas employee (as of Dec 6, 2024)," she said.
Suhaidah said this while testifying in the trial of Khairul Akmal, who is accused of attempting to disclose confidential Petronas documents to Petros in June 2024.
The witness said Khairul Akmal had demonstrated excellent work performance throughout his service and was categorised as "Top Talent" within Petronas' finance division.
"Khairul Akmal also had in-depth knowledge and understanding of the factors affecting the value of oil and gas, as well as the gas value chain.
"The RM15,000 salary received by Khairul Akmal was based on Petronas' internal equity principles for the position of manager.
"However, he had verbally expressed his desire to be transferred to Sarawak as his family lives there," she said.
However, during cross-examination by defence lawyer Louis Liaw, the witness admitted that she was unsure who had written and sent the email containing the confidential documents to the Petros CEO and CFO.
Liaw: After you informed Jumsuri that there was no record of Khairul resigning, any further investigation into who sent the email would have fallen under Jumsuri's jurisdiction, correct?
Suhaidah:
Correct.
Liaw: You did not open the laptop after that to check whether the email had been sent by Khairul, correct?
Suhaidah
: No.
Liaw: This means that when you stated in your witness statement that the email was "sent by Khairul to Datuk Janin Girie and Azha Jalil", you said that based on the email shown in the exhibit, correct?
Suhaidah:
Correct, based on the evidence presented here.
Liaw: So, you saw the email and concluded that it had been sent by Khairul to Janin Girie and Azha Jalil, correct?
Suhaidah:
Correct, based on this email.
Liaw: As to who actually wrote the email and then pressed "send", you do not know?
Suhaidah:
Yes, correct. I am not sure.
On April 18 last year, Khairul Akmal, 41, claimed trial to a charge of attempting to disclose confidential documents relating to Petronas' operational and financial performance to Petros in June 2024.
He was charged with attempting to disclose information contained in a document titled "Q1 2024 Upstream Business Performance Operational & Financial" to Petros.
The document had allegedly been obtained in the course of his duties as Petronas business unit performance manager.
The offence was allegedly committed at a condominium unit in Jalan Pinang here between 3.19pm and 3.21pm on June 8, 2024.
Khairul Akmal faces a maximum fine of RM1 million or imprisonment of up to one year, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Noor Syafina Radzuan prosecuted the case.  The trial before Judge Mazuliana Abdul Rashid continues on Nov 18.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vietnam stocks fall 2.2pct in first week after  FTSE market upgrade
Article:
HANOI: Vietnam's benchmark fell 2.2 per cent in the first week after the country's formal inclusion in FTSE Russell's secondary emerging market index, according to LSEG data.
The decline more than offset last week's one per cent gain, with foreign investors selling more shares than they had bought in anticipation of the Sept 21 reclassification.
Foreign investors, who had been widely expected to increase their exposure after the upgrade, instead sold a net 2.8 trillion dong (US$107.78 million) worth of shares on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange, bourse data showed, after purchasing a net 2.7 trillion dong in the previous week.
The index's decline wiped about US$7.4 billion off its market value up until Sept 24 this week, HoSE data showed.
Since the start of the year, foreign investors havecut their exposure to Vietnamese stocks by nearly US$37 billion.
"The upgrade is only one factor. It does not mean capital will immediately flow into Vietnam," said Hoang Huy, equity strategist at Maybank Securities Vietnam. "Right now, interest rates remain the most important factor for the equity market," Huy added.
The transition will take place over four stages through 2027, with 10 per cent of Vietnam's weighting added in September, an additional 20 per cent in March, and 35 per cent each in June and September next year.
FTSE Russell has estimated the inclusion could redirect up to US$6 billion into Vietnam over time. Asset management firm Vanguard said it planned to invest about US$2.5 billion over the next year.
Despite optimism about the upgrade, Vietnam's benchmark VN-Index has lost about 0.5 per cent this year, lagging gains of roughly 27 per cent in Thailand and 23 per cent in Singapore, according to LSEG data.
Last year, however, Vietnam was among Southeast Asia's best-performing stock markets as investors positioned themselves for the expected FTSE reclassification.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia strengthens bonds with Central Asian countries in higher education
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Central Asian countries are set to strengthen cooperation in higher education, with a focus on student and academic mobility, as well as research and university partnerships.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir is in Astana, Kazakhstan, for a working visit until Sunday (Sept 27) to attend the Malaysia-Central Asia Ministerial Higher Education Meeting.
The meeting is the first between Malaysia's Higher Education Minister and higher education ministers from Central Asian countries, opening the way for closer cooperation between higher-learning institutions in both regions.
"Central Asia has a great scholarly tradition and untapped potential that we should explore together.
"This meeting is an initial step towards connecting the strengths of Malaysian universities, researchers and the younger generation with the region," Zambry said in a statement today.
The visit will also see the Malaysia-Central Asia Higher Education Forum 2026, which will bring together higher education leaders and representatives to discuss student and academic mobility, research collaboration and university partnerships.
Zambry is also scheduled to receive an honorary professorship from L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University and deliver a public lecture at the university.
Up to June, some 3,726 students from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan were pursuing their studies at public and private higher education institutions in Malaysia.
The ministry said the visit reflected its commitment to expanding Malaysia's international higher education network and building long-term cooperation with Central Asian countries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rupiah set for biggest weekly fall since May as higher US yields, stronger dollar bite
Article:
SINGAPORE: Indonesia's rupiah was set for its biggest weekly fall since late May on Friday, pressured by rising US Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and expectations that US interest rates will remain higher for longer.
The rupiah extended losses, weakening as much as 0.3 per cent to 17,935 per dollar on the day. It has declined nearly one per cent so far this week. Bank Indonesia on Wednesday kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 5.75 per cent, after raising it by a cumulative 100 basis points between May and June to support the weakening rupiah.
The central bank signalled it would rather support the rupiah through market-based measures as elevated oil prices and higher US yields pressure the currency.
Although the rate hold was understandable, "the market is looking for stronger signals that BI will prioritise rupiah stability," said Lukman Leong, chief analyst at Doo Financial Futures.
A more credible fiscal policy, central bank intervention and stronger foreign capital inflows are needed to put the rupiah on a more sustained recovery path, Leong said.
The rupiah has been the worst performer among emerging Asian currencies, falling seven per cent as fuel subsidies aimed at shielding consumers from soaring oil prices have added to fiscal strains and heightened concerns over the government's expansive spending plans.
The outlook for domestic capital flows also adds to the rupiah's vulnerability, Leong said, pointing to recent weakness in Indonesian equities.
The benchmark Jakarta Composite Index was down 0.6 per cent on the day and more than 27 per cent year-to-date. Among other regional currencies, the Thai baht and the Indian rupee traded flat.
The broader mood remained cautious as a sharp overnight rise in oil prices pushed 30-year US Treasury yields to their highest since 2004, while a stronger dollar continued to weigh on regional currencies.
The US dollar has climbed more than one per cent so far this week, hitting a two-month high and heading for its first back-to-back weekly gains since June. The Malaysian ringgit, the South Korean won and Taiwan's dollar rebounded from Thursday's losses, strengthening between 0.3 per cent and 0.7 per cent.
Regional equity markets ticked higher, with China, South Korea and Taiwan closed for holidays. Stocks in Thailand and the Philippines rebounded from the previous session's losses, rising 0.4 per cent and 1.7 per cent, respectively, while equities in Singapore added 0.5 per cent.
"Markets today appear to be in a holding pattern, with lighter trading volumes as several key Asian markets are closed for holidays, helping regional equities absorb the rise in oil yields without a sharp risk-off move," said Gary Tan, portfolio manager for emerging market equities at Allspring Global Investments.
Investors were also monitoring a summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington amid no signs of breakthroughs on thorny issues such as AI, trade and Taiwan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran puts seven-day timeline on reopening Strait of Hormuz
Article:
NEW YORK: Iran has submitted a proposal to the United States to end their war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, its foreign minister told media outlets in New York.
"If certain conditions are met, the strait will be open within seven days and talks will start," Abbas Araghchi, who is in the US for the UN General Assembly, told media outlets including the New York Times and The Guardian.
Japanese news agency Kyodo was the first to report the proposal, citing a senior Iranian official on Tuesday.
Iranian media, however, denied the Kyodo report, while authorities in Teheran have not clarified their position.
Araghchi also met for talks on Tuesday with US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff.
Iran has previously set out seven conditions for ending the war and reopening the strait.
According to Araghchi, as quoted by the New York Times, the latest plan calls for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East for seven days, including in Lebanon.
It also calls for the release of frozen Iranian assets estimated to be worth at least US$12 billion, as well as the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade of Iran.
On the seventh day of the truce, Iran would reopen Hormuz.
Araghchi said he was waiting for a US response to the plan and maintained that China supported the proposal.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting the United States this week where he is meeting with Trump for talks.
Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of Iran's military, told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Teheran's demands.
The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, reopen the strait and launch talks on Iran's nuclear programme.
But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.
Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.
Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar thanks Cherok Tokun community for helping with brother's funeral
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim thanked members of the public and community leaders who attended and helped with the funeral arrangements for his late brother, Idrus Ibrahim.
"Thank you to the people of Cherok Tokun who offered their help.
"Thank you also to friends who came. Thank you very much," Anwar told reporters after Idrus was laid to rest.
Anwar had earlier taken time to personally greet and thank those who attended the funeral.
He later joined hundreds at the Cherok Tokun Bawah Muslim Cemetery for Idrus' burial after Friday prayers.
The sombre gathering was attended by Anwar's children, close family members, villagers and community leaders who came to offer their condolences to the bereaved family.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he had returned to his hometown with a heavy heart to join his extended family in paying their final respects to his elder brother.
Reflecting on the loss, Anwar expressed gratitude for Idrus' lifelong dedication, love and kindness towards the family.
"Thank you for all the love, contributions, and goodwill you poured out for this family throughout your life," he wrote.
Anwar said despite the loss and the absence left by his brother, the family would remain strong and move forward together.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreigner fined RM3,000 for attempted wallet theft at Penang airport
Article:
BALIK PULAU: A Chinese national was fined RM3,000 by the magistrate's court after pleading guilty to attempting to steal a wallet from a man's backpack at the Penang International Airport.
Magistrate Chia Huey Ting ordered Chen Bangjun, 55, to serve three months' jail if he fails to pay the fine.
He was charged under Section 379 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 511, for attempting to steal the wallet between 9.25am and 10am at the airport on Sept 17.
Section 379 provides for up to seven years' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction, while Section 511 limits the jail term for an attempted offence to half of the maximum sentence.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Sofi Jaafar urged the court to pass a deterrent sentence.
Defence counsel Teh Yi Kai requested a lenient sentence as Chen was unemployed and was remorseful after spending nine days in remand.
"Given this was only an attempted theft, there was no actual loss reported, and the accused admitted that the act was driven by greed," Teh said in mitigation.
The court then imposed the RM3,000 fine in default of three months' jail.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor to explore more support for stressed doctors and nurses
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government will look into ways to ease the pressure on doctors and nurses serving in hospitals in the state.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said his administration was open to coordinating mental health and welfare assistance for healthcare workers facing stress.
"The current focus is on what interventions we can provide, starting with support for doctors, medical teams and nurses," he said during a question-and-answer session for the 2027 Selangor Budget.
Responding to a call from a government hospital doctor for the state to monitor stress levels among healthcare personnel, Amirudin said engagement with stakeholders was necessary.
"We need to discuss what specific support you require to ensure the assistance given is effective."
He said stress among healthcare workers may not be caused solely by workload.
"For instance, support could come in the form of housing. We can look into Smart Sewa rental quotas or internal support mechanisms to offer care for those facing difficulties within the existing state government ecosystem.
"We already have mental health support mechanisms in place. Public Health and Environment executive councillor Jamaliah Jamaluddin can look into ways to support doctors experiencing such stress," he said.
Separately, Amirudin said the state government would explore the potential of Universiti Selangor's (Unisel) medical college to help supply nursing graduates to public hospitals in Selangor from next year, shifting from its previous focus on private healthcare institutions.
"We're facing a shortage of nurses. Although healthcare falls under the purview of the Health Ministry, the state government can still play a role in supporting Selangor's healthcare ecosystem," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Thank you, Cikgu': Steven Sim pays tribute to late headmaster, brother of PM Anwar
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim paid a moving tribute to his former primary school headmaster, the late Idrus Ibrahim.
Idrus was the elder brother of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
As he sat beside Idrus' remains, Sim recalled a vivid memory from 35 years ago when the educator pulled his sideburns outside the headmaster's office and warned him to keep his hair neat.
"When you grow up, Cikgu Idrus told me, if you cannot manage small matters properly, you will end up being negligent when dealing with big and important responsibilities," Sim recalled.
Sim said that from his primary school days through to his time as a member of parliament and Cabinet minister, Idrus never stopped offering guidance.
Although students viewed him as strict and fierce at the time, Sim said he later realised that the headmaster simply held high hopes for the personal development and success of every pupil.
"Class, stand up. Thank you, Cikgu," Sim said in his tribute.
"You will always remain in our hearts, our Headmaster, sir."
Idrus, 83, died peacefully at his home in Cherok Tokun, leaving behind cherished memories in the close-knit village community where he spent his life.
Anwar
had earlier arrived

Title: Zahid: Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council established, first meeting in October
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has announced the establishment of the Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council to strengthen halal diplomacy between the two countries.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the council would be chaired by Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organizing Agency (BPJPH), while Malaysia would serve as its secretary-general.
Its first meeting is scheduled to be held in October.
"Next month, the focus will be on facilitating halal certification between Malaysia and Indonesia to streamline bilateral halal trade between the two countries," he said in his speech at the Global Halal Summit 2026 here today.
He said Malaysia and Indonesia signed a memorandum of cooperation in 2023, while bilateral negotiations to facilitate halal certification and trade between the two countries were concluded in June this year.
He said closer cooperation would help identify practical ways to facilitate trade, reduce duplication and connect companies with regional supply chains.
According to Zahid, Malaysia had experience in standards, governance, Islamic finance and trade facilitation, while Indonesia had strengths in scale, production capacity and entrepreneurship.
"The goal of halal diplomacy is for both sides to leverage the trust that has been built to open markets, facilitate investment and create opportunities together," he said.
Zahid said the cooperation should ultimately translate into fewer barriers, easier market access and more companies engaging in cross-border trade.
He said small-scale producers needed clearer pathways to find overseas buyers, while companies that had obtained halal certification should be given the necessary support to fulfil their first export orders.
"The future of halal depends on how well we can connect with one another and build that trust going forward," he said, adding that Malaysia aimed to increase halal exports to about RM80 billion by 2030.
Zahid said the halal industry contributed about 11 per cent to Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP), but only about 14.7 per cent of companies with halal certification were exporters.
"To realise our aspirations, we need to help more of these companies compete overseas. Certification is only the beginning of that journey.
"Companies also need consistent production, suitable packaging, working capital, reliable logistics and an understanding of their target markets," he said.
Meanwhile, Zahid said the Malaysia International Halal Showcase (Mihas) 2026 had attracted potential sales worth US$1.2 billion during the first two days of the event.
MIHAS 2026 is organised by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) and managed by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade), and is being held from Sept 23 to 26, 2026.
Zahid hoped sales and potential sales would continue to increase until MIHAS ends on Sunday, describing the annual event as a global halal exhibition brand despite several other countries also hosting similar showcases.

Title: Italy regulator closes P&G hair removal device probe after ad commitments
Article:
ROME: Italy's antitrust authority (AGCM) said on Friday it had closed its investigation into US consumer goods maker Procter & Gamble's claims for a hair removal device, after the company committed to address the regulator's concerns.
The AGCM opened an investigation in February into the allegedly misleading advertisements for the Braun Skin i-Expert pulsed light epilator, considering them exaggerated and not adequately demonstrated.
P&G committed to remove the claim that the device could leave users free of body hair for two years, the watchdog said.
The group also agreed to extend for a further six months, until the end of December, its 100-day full purchase-price refund guarantee if the product is returned, the regulator added. — REUTERS

Title: What is 'Taiwan independence' and what does that mean for Trump and Xi?
Article:
TAIPEI: China's Xi Jinping told President Donald Trump on Thursday that he hoped the US will adhere to the "correct position" of opposing Taiwan independence, and that the Chinese stance on "reunification" is clear-cut.
Below are some questions and answers about what is meant by the term "Taiwan independence" and the positions of the Chinese, US and Taiwanese governments.
WHAT IS TAIWAN'S HISTORY AND FORMAL NAME TODAY?
The Qing dynasty incorporated Taiwan as part of Fujian province in 1684 and only declared it a separate Chinese province in 1885.
Following the Qing's defeat in a war with Japan, it became a Japanese colony in 1895. In 1945, it was handed over to the Republic of China government at the end of World War Two.
In 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong's Communist forces, the Republic of China government fled and moved its capital to Taiwan, and Republic of China remains the island's formal name.
Mao set up the People's Republic of China, and claimed it was the only legitimate Chinese government for the whole of China, including Taiwan, as the Republic of China's successor state.
WHAT IS TAIWAN'S INTERNATIONAL STATUS AND CHINA'S POSITION?
For decades, the Republic of China in Taipei also claimed to be the legitimate Chinese government, but in 1971 Beijing took over the China seat at the United Nations from Taipei.
Most major Western countries and US allies maintain close unofficial ties with Taiwan by recognising the Republic of China passport and having de facto embassies in each other's capitals.
China says it will not renounce the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control. Beijing has offered Taiwan a "one country, two systems" model similar to Hong Kong, which promised the city a high degree of autonomy, although no major political party in Taiwan supports that.
WHAT IS THE US POSITION?
Any change in official US wording on Taiwan would upend decades of policy set by both Republican and Democratic presidents.
The US severed official ties with Taipei in favour of Beijing in 1979 but is bound by the Taiwan Relations Act to provide the island with the means to defend itself. The US officially takes no position on Taiwan's sovereignty under Washington's "One China" policy.
In 2022, the State Department also added wording on the Six Assurances, referring to six Reagan-era security assurances given to Taiwan, which the United States declassified in 2020.
Among the assurances made in 1982, but never previously formally made public, are statements that the US has not set a date for ending arms sales to Taiwan, nor agreed to prior consultation with Beijing on such sales, or to revise the Taiwan Relations Act that underpins US policy towards the island.
China has repeatedly demanded that the US end arms sales to Taiwan.
In May after meeting Xi in Beijing, Trump said he was still considering whether to go ahead with new weapons sales and that the US was "not looking to have somebody say, 'Let's go independent because the United States is backing us'."
The US ended its formal defence alliance with Taiwan in 1979 and has since then had a policy of "strategic ambiguity" on whether it would come to Taipei's defence should Beijing attack.
IS TAIWAN EFFECTIVELY ALREADY AN INDEPENDENT COUNTRY?
Taiwan, whose people elect their own leaders and whose government controls a defined area of territory with its own military, passport and currency, enjoys de facto independence even if that is not formally recognised by most countries.
Taiwan's government says the Republic of China is a sovereign state and that Beijing has no right to speak for or represent it given the People's Republic of China has no say in how it chooses its leaders and has never ruled Taiwan.
COULD TAIPEI DECLARE A "REPUBLIC OF TAIWAN"?
It would be very difficult and require parliamentary approval of a constitutional amendment and then a referendum, rather than a simple declaration by President Lai Ching-te.
At least 75% of lawmakers would need to pass that amendment, and the ruling Democratic Progressive Party and main opposition party the Kuomintang (KMT) currently have an equal number of seats.
The DPP, which has been in power since 2016, has not made an attempt to change the constitution. The KMT strongly opposes any attempts to change the name Republic of China.
WHAT DOES TAIWAN'S PRESIDENT SAY ABOUT INDEPENDENCE?
China detests Lai and calls him a "separatist." Before Lai was elected president he made comments about being a "practical worker for Taiwan independence." Lai maintains he simply meant Taiwan is already an independent country. - Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka election flood risk remains low, says meteorologist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The risk of major flooding during the Melaka election, expected in November, is low, but monsoon surges must be monitored, a meteorologist says.
Universiti Malaya (UM) meteorologist Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Azizan Abu Samah said November marked the start of the Northeast Monsoon, which generally brought more rain, but this did not necessarily mean flooding in Melaka.
He said weather conditions during the election would also be influenced by the El Niño phenomenon, which could reduce the risk of prolonged rain that could cause major flooding.
"November has already entered the Northeast Monsoon season. So, generally, it is the rainy season, although we are also influenced by El Niño.
"So, the risk of rainfall that could lead to major flooding is low. There may be flash floods, but if voters go to the polls in the morning, I do not think there will be much of an issue with rain," he said when contacted here today.
Last Tuesday, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly to pave the way for the 16th state election.
The Melaka state legislative assembly has 28 seats and its current term was originally scheduled to end on Dec 31.
Azizan said weather conditions would need to be monitored based on developments at the time, as monsoon surges might or might not occur on polling day.
"Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has extensive experience in monitoring and forecasting monsoon surges, enabling early warnings to be issued if such conditions are expected.
"Computerised forecasts by MetMalaysia on monsoon surges can provide an indication about four to seven days in advance.
"The forecast period for heavy rain is shorter and is generally more useful within about 48 to 72 hours before an event," he said.
He said monsoon surges could generally be detected several days in advance based on changes in atmospheric pressure systems, including the development of high pressure over Siberia and China.
"MetMalaysia's ability to forecast monsoon surges has also improved through years of monitoring the phenomenon," he said.
However, Azizan said it was still too early to determine the weather specifically on polling day as the election date had yet to be set.
"November is still some time away. We can give an indication of the season, but we cannot say when, where or what time it will rain," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KEB signs underwriting agreement ahead of ACE Market IPO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KEB Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with M&A Securities Sdn Bhd ahead of its initial public offering (IPO) on the ACE Market.
The IPO comprises a public issue of 138.54 million new shares and an offer for sale of 88.24 million existing shares, totalling 226.78 million shares.
Of the public issue, 44.12 million shares, or five per cent of the company's enlarged share capital, will be allocated to the Malaysian public, while 22.06 million shares, or 2.5 per cent, are earmarked for eligible directors, employees and individuals who have contributed to the group's success.
Another 22.06 million shares, or 2.5 per cent, will be placed with Bumiputera investors, while the remaining 50.3 million shares, or 5.7 per cent, are reserved for private placement to selected investors.
KEB managing director Datuk Lim Kim Chong said the IPO marked an important step in strengthening the company's platform for future growth.
"It will support our plans to expand our development pipeline, acquire additional landbank and enhance our financial flexibility as we continue delivering value-accretive property developments," he said.
Proceeds from the public issue will be used for landbank acquisition, working capital for project development, repayment of bank borrowings and listing expenses.
M&A Equity Holdings Bhd's Datuk Bill Tan said KEB was well positioned to leverage the listing for its next phase of growth.
"We are pleased to formalise this underwriting agreement with KEB as the group advances towards its proposed ACE Market listing," he said.
KEB has more than two decades of experience in residential, industrial, commercial and mixed-use property development.
Its in-house construction arm, KEB Utama Sdn Bhd, is a CIDB Grade G7 registered contractor, allowing the group greater oversight of project execution, quality and delivery timelines.
KEB has completed 14 property development projects to date.
Its development pipeline comprises two ongoing projects with a combined estimated gross development value of RM773.29 million and four future projects worth an estimated RM940.74 million.

Title: PNB targets RM15bil green investments under enhanced framework
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) is targeting RM15 billion in green and transition asset investments by 2030, building on the RM8.1 billion already invested as it strengthens its sustainability agenda.
The country's largest fund manager is also targeting RM500 million in social investments under its enhanced Sustainability Framework 2026 (SF 2026).
SF 2026 sets 16 measurable environmental, social and governance (ESG) targets across its investments, operations and stewardship activities.
PNB said SF 2026 builds on its 2022 sustainability framework and aims to strengthen long-term resilience while ensuring that the value created from Malaysians' savings benefits future generations.
Under SF 2026, PNB has identified three strategic anchors: story pension WISHadvancing organisational sustainability, responsible stewardship and strengthening the nation-building agenda.
Under organisational sustainability, PNB will maintain net-zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, while working towards its longer-term aspiration of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.
It will also seek to reduce indirect emissions from business travel, strengthen sustainable procurement and improve accessibility and inclusivity across its premises and services.
For responsible stewardship, PNB will focus on portfolio decarbonisation, climate resilience, nature and biodiversity, as well as fair and equitable employment practices, including labour and living wage principles.
PNB said these measures are intended to strengthen the resilience and long-term competitiveness of companies in which Malaysians' savings are invested.
The third anchor, strengthening the nation-building agenda, focuses on social and financial inclusion and social investment.
Initiatives will include talent development, scholarships, community investment, financial literacy and heritage preservation.
PNB president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli said the new framework represents a continuation of the sustainability work undertaken since 2022.
"Sustainability has always been integral to how PNB fulfils its mandate. When we introduced our sustainability framework in 2022, we made a deliberate commitment to turn our sustainability ambitions into measurable action.
"Now, we have progressively achieved eight of the 10 targets we set and made meaningful progress across our broader sustainability agenda," he said.
Among the milestones, PNB said it achieved its Net Zero Enterprise 2025 target, with 100 per cent of its electricity use supported by renewable energy certificates for PNB Enterprise.
It has also invested RM8.1 billion in green and transition assets.
Rizal said SF 2026 was "not a reset, but a progression", with greater emphasis on responsible investment, long-term stewardship, social impact and nation building.
"As an institution entrusted with the savings of millions of Malaysians, we must ensure that the value we create endures across generations, while contributing to a more resilient, inclusive and sustainable Malaysia," he said.
PNB said the framework reflects its approach of linking responsible investment with broader economic and social outcomes, including stronger businesses, economic opportunities, financial inclusion and social development.
The framework is anchored by the statement "Investing Responsibly, Empowering Generations" and includes commitments extending to 2030 and beyond.

Title: Anwar's brother laid to rest in Cherok Tokun
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's elder brother, Idrus Ibrahim, was laid to rest at the Cherok Tokun Bawah Muslim Cemetery after Friday prayers.
Amid gloomy weather, hundreds of mourners gathered to pay their final respects.
The cemetery is about 50m from Idrus' house.
The sombre gathering included Anwar, his children, close family members, villagers, community leaders and dignitaries who arrived to offer condolences to the bereaved family.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he returned to his hometown with a heavy heart to join his extended family in paying their final respects to his elder brother.
Reflecting on the loss, Anwar expressed deep gratitude for his late brother's lifelong dedication, love and kindness towards the family.
"Thank you for all the love, contributions, and goodwill you poured out for this family throughout your life," he shared in a heartfelt message.
Despite the overwhelming sense of loss and irreplaceable absence left in their lives, the prime minister reaffirmed the family's strength and resolve to move forward together.

Earlier, at 12.20pm, Anwar joined local villagers on foot, walking about 200m from Idrus' residence to the temporary prayer hall of Masjid Cherok Tokun Bawah.
Anwar walked alongside the community to accompany the remains for Friday prayers and funeral prayers, which were presided over by Penang mufti Datuk Dr Mohd Sukki Othman, before proceeding with the burial.
Idrus, 83, passed away peacefully at his home in Cherok Tokun, leaving behind cherished memories in the close-knit village community where he spent his life.

Title: Google prepares to test AI chips in space
Article:
SAN JOSE (California): Google will launch a prototype satellite to evaluate how its artificial intelligence (AI) chips perform in space, the company said on Thursday, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
"In low Earth orbit, satellites can access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth," Google said in a blog post.
"Eventually, it could be possible to link together multiple constellations of satellites, allowing them to manage larger AI workloads while in orbit."
Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) will be loaded onto a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket next week to test how they handle the "physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space", Google said.
"Some things can only be tested in space ... This first launch is about seeing what works, identifying points of failure, and applying those findings to future missions."
Cooling orbital data centres and ensuring that the satellites can communicate at very high bandwidth over extremely short distances are also "engineering hurdles", the company said.
"Exploring space as a viable location for scalable AI compute won't happen all at once. It takes methodical engineering, starting with proving our hardware can handle the physical and unpredictable realities of operating in orbit." — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka channels RM196m into schools, education aid for 140,000 children
Article:

Title: 4 Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Four locations in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm, with Serian recording the highest reading at 174.
After weeks of choking haze affecting the country, Sarawak was the only state with areas in the unhealthy category.
The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Kuching recorded 162, followed by Samarahan at 161 and Sri Aman at 156.
Elsewhere, Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded a reading at 90, followed by Sarikei at 87, Bintulu at 86, and Larkin in Johor and Kapit at 85 each.
In the Klang Valley, Shah Alam recorded 83, Johan Setia 80 and Cheras 78, all within the moderate range.
Three areas recorded good air quality: Tanah Merah in Kelantan at 46, Langkawi in Kedah at 38 and Besut in Terengganu at 30.
An API reading of 0 to 50 is considered good, 51 to 100 moderate and 101 to 200 unhealthy.

Title: Haze forces Kuching Marathon 2026 cancellation at eleventh hour
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 25 — The Kuching Marathon 2026 scheduled for Sunday (September 27) has been cancelled due to the prevailing haze situation affecting Kuching and surrounding areas.
In announcing the cancellation, the Kuching Marathon Association (KMA) said it had been continuously monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and other environmental indicators since the onset of the haze.
It said the decision was made after consultation with relevant authorities and medical advisers, with the health and safety of participants, crew members, volunteers, officials, medical teams, and the public taking precedence.
“To honour the commitment of our runners, all registered participants may collect their finisher medal and finisher tee starting tomorrow at Plaza Merdeka Shopping Centre (Alfresco Area),” KMA said in a statement.
It added that detailed collection schedules and instructions would be announced on its official social media platforms.
The cancellation came shortly after State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah visited the Kuching Marathon registration and race pack collection at Plaza Merdeka.
Map shows the route for what would have been the 42km full marathon. — Picture from Facebook/Kuching Marathon via The Borneo Post
When met by reporters, Abdul Karim had said the decision on whether the marathon could proceed would depend on the prevailing haze situation and assessments by the relevant authorities.
Abdul Karim, who is also State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister, said the State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) had established indicators based on API readings to determine whether outdoor events could be safely held.
“I’m not in the capacity to say yes or no for the race to be conducted, because we in Sarawak do have the SDMC to determine whether an outdoor event should be held or not,” he said.
He also said more than 13,000 participants had registered for this year’s Kuching Marathon.
The first Kuching Marathon was held on August 17, 2014, and has since grown into one of Borneo’s largest international mass-participation running events.
Participation grew rapidly, surpassing 10,000 runners by 2019, with subsequent editions attracting participants from more than 40 countries. — The Borneo Post

Title: Woman dies after Honda Jazz loses control, crashes into lorry in Kulai
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — A 32-year-old woman with a hearing disability died after the Honda Jazz she was driving crashed into the rear of a lorry at KM32 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Air Hitam here early today.
The woman, who worked as a general worker at a technology park in Kulai, suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, while the 66-year-old local lorry driver sustained minor injuries,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the crash at about 6.15am.
“Initial police investigations found that the accident is believed to have occurred when the Honda Jazz driven by the victim, travelling from Kulai Besar towards Johor Bahru, lost control.
“The woman’s car then crashed into the rear of a lorry driven by a 66-year-old local man who was stopped at a traffic light,” he said in a statement.
Tan said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged anyone with information about the crash to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohd Fatin Mohd Radzi at 018-3649199.

Article:
